verdict.rationale: Datalab ships its own non-interactive surfaces suited to headless automation: a documented CLI (`datalab convert document.pdf --format html`), a Python SDK, REST endpoints with an API-key health check, and webhooks that remove the need for polling. However, nothing in the evidence documents CI usage specifically, so the CI half of the story is only implied by these programmatic interfaces. missing for 10: explicit CI/CD integration docs or examples (e.g., GitHub Actions or env-var auth guidance for pipelines), CLI exit-code/non-interactive behavior documentation, independent hands-on corroboration of headless/CI use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Use the Datalab CLI to convert documents from the command line.
The Datalab Python SDK provides a simple interface for document conversion, pipelines, structured extraction, form filling, and file management.
This endpoint is used to check the health of the API, given an API key.
Webhooks provide real-time notifications when your document processing jobs complete, eliminating the need for continuous polling.
